name: Mesothelioma of the Tunica Vaginalis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Mesothelioma of the Tunica Vaginalis

criteria.description: Identification of malignant mesothelial cells with characteristic morphology in tunica vaginalis tissue biopsy
Positive immunohistochemical staining for mesothelial markers such as calretinin, WT-1, and cytokeratin 5/6
Imaging evidence of hydrocele or mass involving the tunica vaginalis on ultrasound or MRI

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with positive immunohistochemical markers is required; imaging findings support diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of metastatic carcinoma and other paratesticular tumors.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Painless scrotal mass localized to tunica vaginalis
Persistent unilateral hydrocele refractory to standard treatment
searchTerms: one-sided hydrocele not responding to treatment

common.symptomName: Heaviness or discomfort in the scrotum
Firm, irregular tunica vaginalis thickening on palpation
searchTerms: hard thickening felt in scrotal covering

common.symptomName: Hydrocele with septations or nodularity on ultrasound
searchTerms: hydrocele with internal divisions on ultrasound
inflammation of epididymis or spermatic cord

occasional.symptomName: Systemic constitutional symptoms such as weight loss

rare.symptomName: Metastatic spread to regional lymph nodes
searchTerms: cancer spread to nearby lymph nodes
blood in urine from local tumor invasion

laboratory: Elevated serum mesothelin-related peptides (in some cases)
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: Ultrasound showing hydrocele with nodular or papillary projections
MRI demonstrating tunica vaginalis thickening and mass lesions
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; occasional BAP1 mutations reported in mesothelioma
other: Histopathology revealing epithelioid, sarcomatoid, or biphasic mesothelial cell morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of solid nodules or papillary projections on imaging
Lack of malignant cells on cytology or biopsy
Younger age of onset (children and adolescents)
Diffuse testicular involvement rather than tunica vaginalis

redFlags: Firm, irregular scrotal thickening with nodularity
references: Attanoos RL, Gibbs AR. Mesothelioma of the tunica vaginalis testis: a review. Histopathology. 1997;30(4):303-309.
Bianchi M, Bianchi T. Malignant mesothelioma of the tunica vaginalis testis: a review. Urologia. 2014;81(4):222-226.
